data.description:
# Split out of bug beb1 (signing fixed; these two ACs were NOT delivered)

beb1 fixed the review bot's authorship: its events now resolve an author identity and carry an
`author_sig` (verified end-to-end on 39 post-deploy events). Two of its acceptance criteria
were NOT met and are split here rather than ticked.

## 1. creation_channel is still null
Measured after the beb1 deploy: 5 CREATE events from env b2b5c498, `creation_channel` = None on
all 5 — unchanged from the 8880 pre-fix events. Signing and channel-stamping are independent:
fixing the git identity resolved author/author_id/author_sig but did nothing for
creation_channel. Investigate why the channel is not inferred/passed on the reviewbot's
create path, and decide the correct value for a bot-authored ticket.

## 2. Nothing makes an identity-less or unsigned writer LOUD
This is why beb1 ran for a month undetected. The failure was silent at three layers:
- `_seam` gates on `if author_id and signing_key` — a null author_id skips signing with NO log
  line at all;
- when it IS reached, a signing failure is only a logger.warning in a container whose logs
  nobody reads;
- identity.require_authenticated is False (advisory), so nothing fails.
It surfaced only via an unrelated audit of an fsck tally.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Review-bot CREATEs carry a non-null `creation_channel`.
- [ ] fsck reports any env_id whose events are 0% signed (or authored 'Unknown') as a counted
      issue — the per-env signed-rate breakdown that found beb1 was a one-off script and
      should be a standing check.
- [ ] `_seam` logs when signing is SKIPPED for lack of an identity, not only when it FAILS —
      the skip path is currently silent.
- [ ] Held-out test for each.
data.title: Review-bot CREATEs still carry creation_channel=null; no guard makes an unsigned writer loud
